survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICILS 2018 used a complex, multi-stage cluster sampling design with stratification: schools were selected with PPS systematic sampling (and explicit stratification where applicable), and within schools students and teachers were selected using systematic stratified sampling via IEA WinW3S. Sampling weights were computed as products of base (design) weights and non-response adjustment factors at each relevant stage, yielding final student weights (TOTWGT) and analogous final teacher weights (TOTWGT). Non-response adjustments redistributed weights within explicit strata under an assumption of non-informative response within adjustment cells. For variance estimation, the report specifies jackknife repeated replication (JRR) as the method for sampling variance; however, replicate-weight variable names are not provided in the extracted text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This technical report primarily documents ICILS 2018 sampling, field operations, data management, and scaling procedures rather than estimating a predictive model with a clearly defined dependent variable for which plausible values (PVs) and missing-data handling choices are reported in an analysis section. While the report describes that CIL and CT achievement statistics were derived using Rasch scaling and that PVs were generated with full conditioning, it does not provide an empirical ML analysis pipeline with explicit PV-combining and missing-data handling decisions for a specific outcome model. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are not reported at the level required for extraction of an analysis strategy.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: ICILS 2018 targeted grade 8 students (mean age at least 13.5) and sampled students within sampled schools using IEA WinW3S. School-level exclusions removed very small schools and special-needs schools (and other country-specific exclusions) prior to sampling; within-school exclusions applied to students with disabilities or insufficient language proficiency. Participation in the final database required that students responded to at least one task in the achievement test; schools were treated as non-participants for student data if survey procedures were not followed (e.g., incomplete listing/coverage), and for teacher data if fewer than 50% of sampled teachers participated. Replacement schools were used only for limited non-response at the school level, and replacement was not permitted at the individual level.

data.outcome_summary: ICILS 2018 is an IEA large-scale assessment of lower-secondary students’ computer and information literacy (CIL) and, for participating countries, computational thinking (CT). Students in the target grade (typically grade 8, around age 14) completed computer-based CIL modules (five 30-minute modules with two randomly assigned per student) and, where implemented, two additional CT modules (two 25-minute modules in randomized order). The report documents a two-stage cluster sampling design: schools were selected using stratified PPS systematic sampling, and within schools students and teachers were selected using systematic stratified sampling via IEA WinW3S. Achievement scales were derived using Rasch item response theory, and CIL/CT summary statistics were produced using plausible values with full conditioning; proficiency levels for CIL were developed using scale cut-points. The report also specifies complex survey weighting with non-response adjustments and variance estimation via jackknife repeated replication (JRR), and it details data cleaning, scaling, and quality assurance procedures to support cross-national comparability.
